title: Poulet Roti
subtitle: French roast chicken with tarragon butter
excerpt: A whole chicken rubbed under and over the skin with tarragon butter, roasted until golden and rested properly. The French version does not rush the resting time.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roast chicken is one of the most fundamental dishes of the French home kitchen and bistro. The French technique emphasises very high heat at the start to colour the skin, trussing to keep the bird compact and even, and a generous resting period before carving.

recipeTools.notes: A roasting tin just large enough for the chicken.

content.text: Poulet roti is a whole roast chicken with tarragon butter pushed under the skin, roasted until the skin is deeply golden and the meat is juicy. The French version finishes with a long rest. The juices settle back into the meat during that time, and carving too early is the most common reason a good chicken disappoints.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7.

Mix the softened butter with the tarragon, garlic, 1 teaspoon of the salt, and the pepper. Slide your fingers carefully under the skin of the chicken breast without tearing it and push most of the butter under the skin, smoothing it out. Rub the rest over the outside of the bird.
Season the outside with the remaining salt. Stuff the lemon halves into the cavity. Truss the chicken with kitchen twine if you like, tying the legs together.

Place breast-side up in a roasting tin. Roast at 220 C for 20 minutes until the skin starts to brown, then reduce to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4 and continue for 50 to 60 minutes, basting twice. An instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh should read 75 C.

Tip the chicken so the juices from the cavity run into the tin. Leave to rest on a warm plate, loosely covered with foil, for at least 20 minutes before carving. Use the resting juices to make a quick pan sauce if you like.
